why: A1.1-a1 REGRESSION ANCHOR. Putting owned parameters into the lowering set made `return s` lower as a fresh-factory return, and the core read a fresh return of something it never saw acquired as an escaping borrow: [OWN004] 'parg_N' is a borrow and cannot be returned. Six CI jobs, and the 137-file verdict corpus never saw it, because no corpus case returns its own disposable parameter. The recorded facts pin the fix: Echo's `return` carries var=None. What the return really is, is an ALIAS of the parameter; OwnIR reserves `aliasOf`/`aliased` and has never emitted them, so the frontend claims no owned return rather than asserting a false kind. If this record ever shows `return:s`, the alias gap has been filled by accident instead of on purpose.
